subject: Isolation assumptions & pen test report request — FinBank private deployment
messages:
From: Tom Heller <tom.heller@finbank.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finbank.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pen test report + clarification on boundary assumptions for our private VPC deployment

Jasmine —

Thanks for the demo last week. Security is asking for the most recent penetration test report and a short write-up of the boundary/assumption model for the private deployment you’ll be running in our VPC (network segmentation, what’s inside the customer-managed subnet vs Redwood-managed control plane, any cross-tenant Egress/Ingress paths). They specifically want: 

- Full PT report (executive summary + critical/major findings)
- Which findings relate to customer-managed configuration vs Redwood-managed infrastructure
- Diagram of boundaries and trust zones for our private deployment
- Current remediation status and timelines for open items

Can you send over the artifacts or point me at a secure location? Preferably by COB Friday. We are coordinating with our internal auditors and want to close this before the procurement review.

Best,
Tom
Tom Heller
Director, InfoSec — FinBank Corp
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Tom Heller <tom.heller@finbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + clarification on boundary assumptions for our private VPC deployment

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. We can share the pen test evidence and a boundary diagram. Quick questions to ensure we provide the right artifacts: 

1) Is your procurement team ok with us providing the full vendor PDF (no redactions)? If not, we can provide an executive summary + findings matrix with environment mapping.
2) Which control plane components do you want annotated (control plane admin API, metrics/telemetry egress, onboarding API)?

Plan: I’ll loop in Karthik and Neha from Security to assemble the PT executive summary, remediation tracker, and a VPC boundary diagram showing: customer-managed subnets, Redwood-managed control plane endpoints (in a separate account), and any cross-account network peering or NAT hop assumptions. Expect an initial package today, final package by Friday COB. 

If there’s a preferred secure transfer method (SFTP, customer shared Drive link, or our secured Drive share), tell me and we’ll use that.

Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Request: pen test report + clarification (internal)

Team —

I pulled the artifacts from the security repository: we have a third-party assessment performed 2026-08-15 by RedTeam Labs (summary + full report). Attached: redwood_pt_summary_202608.pdf (exec summary + findings matrix) and vpc_boundary_diagram.png (annotated for private deployments). 

Short status: 
- Critical findings: 0 in the 2026 assessment.
- Major findings: 2 (both related to weak config defaults in the on-prem connector component; remediation completed 2026-09-10 and validated by internal verification).
- Medium/minor: 6 items; 3 are customer-configuration recommendations (eg. restrict SGs, enforce flow logs), 3 are Redwood fixes (completed or scheduled).

Mapping notes for FinBank private deployment: 
- Control plane (API endpoints, orchestration) runs in Redwood-managed account and is accessed over mutually authenticated TLS. No control plane compute is deployed into customer VPC.
- Customer-managed subnets host the inference workers (customer VPC/private deployment) at the customer’s choice of instance types. We establish a short-lived, customer-initiated peering/VPN that we do not transit for other customers.
- Egress assumptions: customer controls NAT/egress; we recommend restricting outbound to the minimal set required for health checks and KV cache retrieval.

I’ll prepare a remediation matrix mapping each finding to either "Customer responsibility" or "Redwood responsibility" and export an unredacted report for TOM if procurement permits.

-Karthik
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Tom Heller <tom.heller@finbank.com>
Cc: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finbank.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + clarification on boundary assumptions for our private VPC deployment

Tom —

Attached is the package we discussed: 
- FINBANK_vpc_assumptions_20260930.pdf — succinct boundary assumptions and recommended customer config checklist.
- redwood_pt_summary_202608.pdf — executive summary and findings matrix (full PDF available on request).
- vpc_boundary_diagram.png — annotated diagram for your private deployment.

Highlights:
- No Redwood compute runs inside customer-managed subnets; our control plane communicates over mTLS endpoints located in our managed account.
- Networking model uses customer-initiated peering/VPN; there is no multi-tenant transit.
- Two high-priority items from the last report were fixed earlier this month; the remediation verification notes are included in the findings matrix.

We’ve uploaded the unredacted full report to a secured Drive folder (link below). If procurement needs a signed copy from RedTeam Labs, we can request that and share via your preferred transfer mechanism.

Secure folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/finbank/pt-evidence-2026

Next steps: 
- Please confirm whether an unredacted full report is acceptable to the procurement/audit team.
- If you want a short (1-page) customer-facing statement mapping each open item to ownership, we can produce that by EOD Friday.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: FINBANK_vpc_assumptions_20260930.pdf (application/pdf), redwood_pt_summary_202608.pdf (application/pdf), vpc_boundary_diagram.png (image/png)
From: Tom Heller <tom.heller@finbank.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finbank.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + clarification on boundary assumptions for our private VPC deployment

Jasmine —

Received, thanks for the quick turnaround and thoroughness. A couple quick clarifying points from our auditors: 

1) On the vpc_boundary_diagram, can you annotate the exact service FQDNs and ports used for health checks / cache retrieval so our network team can pre-authorize egress?
2) For the two items marked as Redwood responsibility, can you provide the verification artifacts (scan results or ticket IDs) showing remediation and the re-test date?

If you can add those annotations to the FINBANK package and re-upload, that will expedite sign-off. Otherwise looks in good shape and procurement will move forward pending the additional artifacts.

Tom
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Tom Heller <tom.heller@finbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report + clarification on boundary assumptions for our private VPC deployment

Tom —

Will do. Karthik/Neha — can you add the FQDN/port table and remediation verification artifacts (tickets: SEC-8764, SEC-8791; internal scan date: 2026-09-12) to the FINBANK_vpc_assumptions_20260930.pdf and re-upload to the secure folder? I’ll confirm once the updated package is live.

Jasmine
